SASRec scores each position against its next-item target and uses the final sequence feature for inference ([reference implementation](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/master/python/model.py)). Recommended causal pooling: let `m = sequence.ne(0)` and `r = m.long().cumsum(1)`. At query position `t`, include position `j` iff `m[j]`, `j <= t`, and `0 <= r[t]-r[j] < k`; average the selected item embeddings using the actual count, clamped to at least one. Mask padding-query outputs to zero. This counts interaction occurrences, preserving repeated IDs. Pool only input history, never positive targets or negatives. Keep transformer attention causal too; causal pooling cannot repair leaked encoder features. For strictly left-padded sequences, a masked trailing-window sum divided by its nonpadding count is equivalent.

Verify the vectorized implementation against a simple loop that explicitly selects each prefix’s last `k` nonzero occurrences. Include repeated IDs, short histories, all-padding inputs, and `k=1`/`k>L`. Compare pooled features and positive/negative logits at every valid training position. Change suffix items after `t` and confirm features/scores through `t` remain unchanged. With `model.eval()` and gradients disabled, compare final-position training-style dot products against inference scores for identical candidate IDs; left padding means the last valid index is `L-1`, not `length-1`. Preserve positional indices when checking prefixes.

Save weights plus architecture/pooling configuration, reload through the generated predictor, and compare identical inputs, candidate order, category routing, and raw scores ([PyTorch checkpoint guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html)). Suggested FP32 acceptance: finite outputs and `assert_close(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)`; report maximum absolute error. Ranking agreement alone can hide scoring inconsistencies.
